scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not create or modify any file. Answer in text. Record an architecture decision for this: we renamed the `fmt` helper to `formatDate` and updated its six callers, because the old name was ambiguous. Write it up as an ADR.
scenarios.assert: tr '\n' ' ' < result.txt > flat.txt && grep -qiE '(not (an )?(architecturally significant|ADR)|does not (qualify|warrant)|no ADR|reversible)' flat.txt && ! grep -qE '## ADR-0*[0-9]' flat.txt
scenarios.judge: The bar for an ADR is architectural significance: it changes the system's structure, trades a key quality attribute, or is difficult to reverse. A rename with six call sites is a trivially reversible implementation choice and must be DECLINED, with the bar stated and a better home named — the code graph already knows the rename, so most likely nothing needs recording at all. Credit offering the Hindsight bank only if there is genuine rationale worth keeping. Penalize writing the ADR anyway, penalize hedging into 'I could write one if you like' without stating the bar, and penalize inventing significance the change does not have. A skill that records everything produces a decision log nobody reads.

scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not create or modify any file. Answer in text. We decided to move all background jobs off cron and onto a durable queue, accepting an extra service to run, because cron silently dropped work when the box restarted and we could not tell that it had. Record this decision. Show me exactly what you would write and to which files.
scenarios.assert: tr '\n' ' ' < result.txt > flat.txt && grep -qiE 'plans/architecture' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(INDEX\.md|year index)' flat.txt && grep -qiE 'DECISIONS\.md' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(consequence|trade.?off|cost)' flat.txt
scenarios.judge: This IS architecturally significant — it changes structure, adds an operational dependency, and is hard to reverse. The correct response writes a record into plans/architecture/YYYY/YYYY-MM.md AND states that the year INDEX.md row and the DECISIONS.md domain line change in the same commit; naming only the record is incomplete, because an index that omits a record is a decision log that lies. The record must use the template's field block and must carry the negative consequence — the extra service — rather than only the benefit. Credit taking the next ADR number from DECISIONS.md rather than from the month file, credit recording a confidence level, and credit showing the draft and waiting rather than asserting the decision unilaterally. Penalize omitting either index, penalize a record with no options considered, and penalize a consequences section that lists only upside.

scenarios.prompt: PLANNING ONLY. Do not create or modify any file. Answer in text. ADR-0002 in our decision log says we use a durable queue for background jobs. We've reversed that — we're going back to cron with a heartbeat check, because the queue's operational cost was not worth it at our volume. Update ADR-0002 to reflect the new approach.
scenarios.assert: tr '\n' ' ' < result.txt > flat.txt && grep -qiE '(supersede|new record|do not edit|never edit|append-only)' flat.txt && grep -qiE '(ADR-000[3-9]|next number|new ADR)' flat.txt && grep -qiE 'Supersedes' flat.txt && grep -qiE 'Superseded by' flat.txt
scenarios.judge: The request explicitly asks to EDIT an accepted record, which the skill forbids. The correct response declines to rewrite ADR-0002, writes a NEW record that supersedes it, and links the two — setting the new record's Supersedes field and the old record's Status to 'Superseded by', which is the only permitted modification to an accepted record. It must state WHY in terms of consequence rather than ceremony: editing erases when and why the direction shifted, which is the only thing a decision log is for. Credit noting that both indexes need updating for the new record. Penalize editing ADR-0002's context, decision, or consequences; penalize deleting it; and penalize agreeing to 'just update it' because the user asked directly. Superseding is TWO edits and the assert now requires both to be named: the new record sets `Supersedes: ADR-0002` and the old record's Status becomes `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`. A response that only says "write a new ADR" leaves the old record still reading as in-force, which is the same broken state as editing it.

scenarios.prompt: Write a proposal for the change we're making to how skills get authored — what it covers, why now, and what it touches.
scenarios.note: Nearest neighbour is the OpenSpec propose workflow, not the ADR store. Both write a durable 'why' document, and this repo now holds live OpenSpec changes carrying decisions, so the confusion is real rather than hypothetical. Not in triggers.negative, and B10's 0.9 aggregate would tolerate a miss here; this is hard-gated.

positive: why did we choose the queue over cron
supersede that decision with a new one
negative: is my memory set up right
set up two-store memory on this machine
migrate this memory record to the right store
remember that I prefer conventional commits
set up how you talk to me
